 BREAKING Sport Scotland under-20s call up three Borderers for friendlies
 By Darin Hutson 
 Published 17th Nov 2026, 10:35 GMT Updated 17th Nov 2026, 10:35 GMT Three Borderers have been selected for a Scotland training squad playing two warm-up matches this month and next ahead of rugby’s 2027 Under-20 Six Nations in February and March.
 Head coach Fergus Pringle has named a squad of 33 for games away to Ireland in Cork this coming Friday, with kick-off at Musgrave Park, alias Virgin Media Park, at 5pm, and at home to Wales at Edinburgh’s Hive Stadium on Friday, December 18.
 Jack Utterson in action for Edinburgh during their 28-26 pre-season friendly loss hosting Ulster at the capital’s Hive Stadium in September (Photo: Ewan Bootman/SNS Group/Edinburgh) Almost half of the youngsters called up are previous under-20 internationals, Kelso’s Jack Utterson and Peebles’ Rory McHaffie being among 16 such players, and the other 17 are new faces.

Utterson, 19, is one of three hookers selected, though he has been fielded as a back-rower on national service previously, and they’re among 18 forwards.
 Rory McHaffie on the ball for Scotland’s under-20s during their 45-26 loss at home to France in March at Edinburgh’s Hive Stadium during rugby’s 2026 Under-20 Six Nations (Photo: Ross Parker/SNS Group/SRU) His Edinburgh academy teammate McHaffie, also 19, is one of four back-three players among the squad’s 15 forwards.
 Utterson has eight prior under-20 caps to his name since February 2025 and McHaffie is on ten over the same timeframe, both of them having helped the age-grade side to five wins.
 The other Borderer called up by former Hawick lock Pringle, 48, is hitherto-uncapped Melrose centre Charlie Robbie.
 Utterson’s fellow forwards are Daniel Cruickshanks, Michael Scarth, Zak Burgess, Boyd Cooper, Jack Nesbitt, Jackson Rennie, Murray Robertson, James Dalrymple, Will May, Archie Appleby, Christian Lindsay, Hamish Mather, Harry Jackaman, Harvey Preston, Jack Kemp, Lloyd Moncrieff and Rory Baxter.
 Charlie Robbie pictured in Glasgow in 2023 (Photo: Melrose RFC) Joining McHaffie and Robbie among the squad’s backs are Adam McKenzie, Gregor Johnston, Struan Talac, Callum Jessop, Henry Widdowson, Ben McDonald, Harry Soboil, Finlay Anderson, Harry Clark, Henry Kesterton, Dan Kelly, Glen Gammell and Rory Caldwell.
 Utterson was part of a week-long combined Edinburgh and Warriors academies training camp in France culminating in a game against Union Bordeaux Begles Espoirs last Tuesday that the visitors won 47-12.
 He was one of ten replacements for that concluding game also including Gala’s Nairn Moncrieff.
 Four other Borderers featured in head coach Henry Pyrgos’s starting line-up – Peebles’ Ross Wolfenden, Gala’s Kerr Johnston and Melrose’s Ben White and Dylan Cockburn.
 The Scots’ under-20s go into 2027’s age-grade Six Nations looking to bounce back from their wooden spoon last time round, on six points from five fixtures.
 They kick off at home to Italy at the Hive on Friday, February 5, and host Wales there a week later.
 They’re away to defending champions France in La Rochelle on Friday, February 19; back home to face Ireland on Thursday, March 4; and they wrap up their campaign on the road in England at Bath on Friday, March 12.
